t: A confederation of four Nahua city-states east of the Valley of Mexico, governed by its rulers and lords in council.
It resisted the Aztec Triple Alliance for generations despite the flower wars and a reported embargo on salt and cotton.
Its alliance with Hernán Cortés in 1519 supplied the warriors and support that brought down Tenochtitlan in 1521.
dyk: Hernán Cortés compared the government of Tlaxcala to those of Venice, Genoa and Pisa, because, he wrote, it had no single supreme ruler.
ev: Traditional date for the foundation of Tlaxcala by Teochichimec migrants
Quiahuixtlan completes the confederation of four altepetl
The Triple Alliance begins the ‘flower wars’ against Tlaxcala and its neighbours
Large-scale war with the Aztecs and Huexotzinco begins under Moctezuma II
Tlaxcala fights Hernán Cortés, then allies with him on 23 September
The Spaniards shelter in Tlaxcala after La Noche Triste and the Battle of Otumba
Tlaxcalan forces help take Tenochtitlan, which falls on 13 August

f.capital: Tlaxcallan (the four altepetl of Tepeticpac, Ocotelolco, Tizatlan and Quiahuixtlan)
f.predecessor: Olmeca-Xicalanca lordships of the Puebla-Tlaxcala Valley
